_comment: Bu dosya DSI-Wiki-Service-Supervisor.py tarafından JSONS/instances/*.json'dan otomatik üretilir — elle düzenlenmez. Bu commit'lenmiş hâli boş şablondur.

documentation.prompt:
Full markdown. Use ALL of these CORE sections, in order, every one present even if a section is just "Not covered in raw source.":
1. Status
2. Problem & Motivation
3. TEC — Technical: architecture, file/directory structure, key classes/functions BY NAME, data flow, algorithms, running services/processes/ports. Name actual files and functions instead of summarizing them away — this is the section most likely to lose detail.
4. Configuration — env vars, config files, ports, credential locations (never values)
5. Usage — concrete examples
6. Known Issues & Limitations
7. Missing Information — anything the raw source didn't cover; use this instead of inventing content for a CORE section you don't have facts for.
Then, ONLY if the raw source actually discusses them (by name, more than once), add matching CONDITIONAL sections — omit entirely otherwise, never add a placeholder for one: ART (visual/art assets, asset pipeline), API (exposed endpoints/contracts), DATA (database schema/data models), DEPLOYMENT (services, ports, infra), INTEGRATIONS (external dependencies).

llm.prompt:
Your ENTIRE output for this layer MUST be either (A) the literal 4-line format below with real values, or (B) a fallback paragraph — nothing else. Do NOT write a bulleted list, do NOT write prose sections, do NOT summarize the documentation in your own words if format (A) applies.

FORMAT (A) — use this whenever the documentation mentions ANY real directory, file/config path, command, or named endpoint/port, even just one:
D:<dir1>,<dir2>,<dir3>
C:<path1>,<path2>
R:<command1>;<command2>
X:<name>=<endpoint>,<name>=<endpoint>
Rules for (A): D=real directories/paths mentioned in the docs, C=real config/env/data file paths mentioned, R=real reference commands mentioned (e.g. `systemctl status ...`, a run script) — text only, never execute them, X=named endpoints/ports/URLs mentioned, written as name=value comma-separated pairs. Output ONLY the lines for prefixes that have real facts — omit a prefix line entirely (do not leave it empty) if the docs have nothing for it. Never invent a value. Output nothing else: no headings, no bullets, no extra sentences.

FORMAT (B) — use ONLY if the documentation contains NONE of directories, config paths, commands, or endpoints/ports at all (i.e. format (A) would be 4 empty lines): write a single plain-prose paragraph, hard max 300 tokens, stating current status.

Example of exact (A) output shape (illustrative values only — always use the REAL facts from the documentation, never these examples):
D:~/CLEANUP/MAIN/DSI-Wiki,~/CLEANUP/DATA/Wiki-BASE
C:~/CLEANUP/MAIN/DSI-Wiki/_Python/IngestService/.env
R:systemctl --user status dsi-wiki-ingest.service
X:api=https://wiki-api.example.com,mcp=https://wiki-mcp.example.com

minified.prompt:
Your ENTIRE output for this layer MUST be either (A) the literal 1-line format below with real values, or (B) a fallback sentence — nothing else.

FORMAT (A) — use whenever the documentation mentions ANY real named endpoint/port/URL:
X:<name>=<endpoint>,<name>=<endpoint>
Write ONLY that one line, using real name=value pairs pulled from the documentation. Never invent a value. No other text.

FORMAT (B) — use ONLY if the documentation mentions no real endpoint/port/URL at all: write one plain sentence, hard max 200 tokens, current status only.

Example of exact (A) output shape (illustrative only, always use REAL facts, never this example):
X:api=https://wiki-api.example.com,mcp=https://wiki-mcp.example.com
